sources.title: Java SE8 private accessibility rules
sources.version_or_date: Java SE8 edition; companion PDF is dated 2015-02-13 with March 2015 maintenance release.
sources.sections_read: Introduction; section 6.6.1 reached through an in-document find.
sources.confirmed: Java SE8 distinguishes access control from name scope and limits private member access to the body of its enclosing top-level class.
sources.limits: The boundary is the enclosing top-level class, so nested classes share access and Java does not supply Swift-style extensions. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C29.json.

sources.title: Scala 2 enclosing-template private and private[this]
sources.version_or_date: Archived Scala 2.11 specification; object-local access has dated historical support in the 2.4 changelog.
sources.sections_read: Modifiers: private, qualified private, private[this], and protected; reached through in-document finds.
sources.confirmed: Unqualified private members are restricted to the enclosing template and its companion; qualified private names an enclosing class or package, while private[this] further limits the receiver.
sources.limits: Ordinary private includes companion access, while private[this] is stricter than simple lexical privacy because it restricts the receiver; neither should be transferred without defining extension and companion relationships. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C29.json.

sources.title: Clang SemaAccess.cpp access-checking implementation
sources.version_or_date: Master branch, displayed blob 9dbb93322b7d4ad7b954d63430b3dbd2284947d0; no dated version verified.
sources.sections_read: SetMemberAccessSpecifier; EffectiveContext construction; HasAccess private branch, reached through in-document finds.
sources.confirmed: The public Clang source attaches access to declarations, gathers enclosing declaration contexts, and compares the access context with the naming class when checking private access.
sources.limits: The code implements C++ ownership, inheritance, and friendship rather than Swift extension semantics; the opened master revision was not dated to the cutoff and was not built or executed. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C29.json.

sources.title: Eiffel secret and selective feature export (ECMA-367)
sources.sections_read: Title page; sections 8.7.12-8.7.15 and export-call validity found in document.
sources.confirmed: The 2006 standard specifies client sets and distinguishes public, selective, and secret export; selected clients' descendants also receive access.
sources.limits: Selective export also reaches descendants of named client classes, and secret features govern qualified calls rather than establishing a strict lexical block boundary; the useful transfer is the access design, not an unchanged Eiffel file model. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C29.json.

sources.title: C# private accessibility plus partial type declarations (ECMA-334)
sources.sections_read: Title page; sections 10.5.2 and 17.1.4 reached through in-document finds.
sources.confirmed: The fourth edition is dated June 2006, defines private member access in terms of the declaring type's program text, and contains partial type declarations.
sources.limits: Partial declarations form one type and therefore do not create separate privacy boundaries between implementation blocks; adopting this model would require deciding whether extensions share that type-wide privilege. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C29.json.

sources.title: C++ private members with explicit friendship (N3337)
sources.version_or_date: HTML rendering of N3337; dated availability confirmed by the original 2012-01-16 N3338 report.
sources.sections_read: Chapter 11 member access control; section 11.3 friendship through in-document find.
sources.confirmed: The N3337 rendering limits private access to members and friends, makes friendship explicit, and distinguishes access restrictions from name visibility.
sources.limits: Access is type-wide and extends to member definitions outside the class body, so it does not by itself isolate different extensions; name visibility and completion filtering require separate treatment. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C29.json.
